prerequisites: Familiarity with algorithms and data structures (from 'Methods of informatics' or 'Principles of programming')
Acquaintance with the Internet as a user
Familiarity with basic concepts of protocol and network architecture
Elementary knowledge of cooperative tasks and deadlocks

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with a thorough understanding of important topics in computer networks, focusing on the application, transport, network, and data link layers of the protocol stack, and providing basic context on the physical layer.
Be familiar with the functioning of the most important building-blocks and protocols of a computer network.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Computer Networks and their applications
Important application-layer protocols (e.g., Telnet, HTTP, SMTP, DNS, DHCP, Gnutella, Chord, Bittorrent, TOR)
Basic elements of a transport layer protocol
Important Internet transport protocols (e.g., UDP, RTP, TCP)
Network layer concerns: routing algorithms, congestion control, quality of service, internetworking
Important network layer Internet protocols (e.g., IPv4, ICMP, ARP, Link State Routing)
Case-study protocols: ALOHA, Ethernet, Berkeley-MAC (BMAC), Time Synchronized Mesh Protocol (TSMP)
Simulating application protocols using Telnet (home exercise)

assessment_methods.method: Exam during the examination period (written, open and closed questions)

assessment_rules: The exam will consist of a total of four questions: two open book questions and two closed book questions. Permitted materials include course material.
bibliography: Computer Networks, 5th Edition, A. Tanenbaum (Dutch or English edition)
Documentation will be made available via Toledo
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
